title.zh: 卷三百五十九 列傳第一百十八 李綱下
title.raw: 卷三百五十九 列傳第一百十八 李綱下 Volume 359 Biographies 118: Li Gang 2

sentences.zh: 李綱 下

translations.literal: Li Gang, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang (continued)

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，除觀文殿學士、湖廣宣撫使兼知潭州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, he was removed to [appointed as] Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, Commissioner for Pacification of Huguang, and concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Shaoxing era, Li Gang was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, Commissioner for Pacification of Huguang, and concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，荊湖江、湘之間，流民潰卒群聚為盜賊，不可勝計，多者至數萬人，綱悉蕩平之。

translations.literal: At that time, between the Yangzi and Xiang in Jinghu, displaced persons and scattered soldiers gathered in groups as bandits, beyond counting; the largest groups reached tens of thousands of men, and Gang completely swept them away and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, displaced refugees and scattered troops between the Yangzi and Xiang in the Jinghu region had banded together as marauders beyond counting; some groups numbered in the tens of thousands. Li Gang pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 上言：「荊湖、國之上流，其地數千里，諸葛亮謂之用武之國。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Jinghu is the upper reaches of the state; its territory extends several thousand li. Zhuge Liang called it a land for wielding arms."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Jinghu lies in the upper reaches of the realm, its territory stretching thousands of li. Zhuge Liang called it a country made for war."

sentences.zh: 今朝廷保有東南，控馭西北。

translations.literal: Now the court holds the southeast and controls and reins in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court holds the southeast and keeps the northwest within its grasp.

sentences.zh: 加鼎、澧、岳、鄂若荊南一帶，皆當屯宿重兵，倚為形勢，使四川之號令可通，而襄、漢之聲援可接，乃有恢復中原之漸。

translations.literal: In addition, Ding, Li, Yue, E, and the region around southern Jing should all station heavy troops, relying on them as strategic positions, so that orders from Sichuan can pass through and reinforcements from Xiang and Han can connect—only then will there gradually be progress toward recovering the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: If, in addition, Ding, Li, Yue, E, and the southern Jing corridor were all garrisoned with heavy forces and used as strategic anchors, orders from Sichuan could flow through and reinforcements from Xiangyang and Hanzhong could link up—only then would recovery of the Central Plain become possible step by step.

sentences.zh: 」議未及行，而諫官徐俯、劉斐劾綱，罷為提舉西京崇福宮。

translations.literal: " Before the proposal could be carried out, remonstrating officials Xu Fu and Liu Fei impeached Gang, and he was dismissed and made Director of the Chongfu Palace in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be implemented, remonstrating officials Xu Fu and Liu Fei impeached Li Gang, and he was dismissed to serve as Director of the Chongfu Palace in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，金人及偽齊來攻，綱具防禦三策，謂：「偽齊悉兵南下，境內必虛。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year, the Jurchens and the puppet Qi came to attack. Gang set forth three strategies for defense, saying: "The puppet Qi has sent all its troops south; its territory within must be empty."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year, the Jurchens and the puppet Qi state launched an attack. Li Gang laid out three defensive strategies, arguing: "The puppet Qi has committed all its forces to the south, so its home territory must be hollow."

sentences.zh: 儻出其不意，電發霆擊，搗潁昌以臨畿甸，彼必震懼還救，王師追躡，必勝之理，此上策也。

translations.literal: If we strike from unexpected quarters, like lightning released and thunder striking, raiding Yingchang to threaten the capital region, they will surely be shaken with fear and return to rescue; the imperial army can pursue and follow up—the logic of certain victory. This is the best strategy.
translations.idiomatic: If we take them by surprise and strike like lightning, raiding Yingchang to threaten the capital region, they will panic and rush back to defend it; our imperial forces can then pursue and follow up—a sure path to victory. That is the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 若駐蹕江上，號召上流之兵，順流而下，以助聲勢，金鼓旌旗，千里相望，則敵人雖眾，不敢南渡。

translations.literal: If the emperor halts on the Yangzi and summons troops from the upper reaches to descend with the current, augmenting our display of force, with drums, gongs, banners, and flags visible across a thousand li, then though the enemy is numerous, they will not dare cross south.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor halted on the Yangzi, summoned troops from upstream to descend with the current, and swelled our display of force until drums, banners, and flags stretched for a thousand li, then even a large enemy force would not dare cross south.

sentences.zh: 然後以重師進屯要害之地，設奇邀擊，絕其糧道，俟彼遁歸，徐議攻討，此中策也。

translations.literal: Then send a heavy force to advance and encamp at vital points, set ambushes to intercept, cut off their supply routes, wait until they flee homeward, and slowly deliberate on attack—this is the middle strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Then a heavy force should advance and encamp at key positions, lay ambushes, cut enemy supply lines, wait until they withdraw, and only then deliberate on a counterattack. That is the middle strategy.

sentences.zh: 萬一借親征之名，為順動之計，使卒伍潰散，控扼失守，敵得乘間深入，州縣望風奔潰，則其患有不可測矣。

translations.literal: If, under the pretext of a personal campaign, one uses it as a plan to move the court, causing the ranks to scatter, losing control of strategic passes, and the enemy seizes the opportunity to thrust deep inward, with prefectures and counties fleeing at the mere rumor—then the disaster will be immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: If, under the pretext of a personal campaign, the court were moved on that excuse, troops scattered, strategic passes lost, and the enemy seized the opening to drive deep inland while prefectures and counties fled at the first alarm, the disaster would be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 往歲，金人利在侵掠，又方時暑，勢必還師，朝廷因得以還定安集。

translations.literal: In past years, the Jurchens' profit lay in plunder, and it was midsummer—they were bound to withdraw their army; the court was thus able to stabilize and settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years the Jurchens came chiefly to plunder, and midsummer heat forced them to withdraw, allowing the court time to stabilize and resettle the realm.

sentences.zh: 今偽齊導之而來，勢不徒還，必謀割據。

translations.literal: Now the puppet Qi guides them here; they will not simply return, but must plan to seize and hold territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now the puppet Qi is leading them south; they will not simply turn back, but intend to carve out and hold territory.

sentences.zh: 奸民潰卒從而附之，聲勢鴟張，苟或退避，則無以為善後之策。

translations.literal: Wicked subjects and scattered soldiers will follow and attach themselves; their momentum will swell like a hawk spreading its wings. If we retreat, there will be no plan for what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked subjects and scattered soldiers will flock to them, and their power will swell unchecked. If we retreat, there will be no way to manage what follows.

sentences.zh: 昔苻堅以百萬眾侵晉，而謝安以偏師破之。

translations.literal: Formerly Fu Jian invaded Jin with a million men, yet Xie An defeated him with a detached force.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Fu Jian invaded Jin with a million men, yet Xie An defeated him with a detached column.

sentences.zh: 使朝廷措置得宜，將士用命，安知北敵不授首於我？

translations.literal: If the court arranges matters properly and officers and soldiers obey orders, who is to say the northern enemy will not surrender their heads to us?
translations.idiomatic: If the court handled matters properly and officers and soldiers obeyed orders, who could say the northern enemy would not surrender to us?

sentences.zh: 顧一時機會所以應之者如何耳。

translations.literal: It all depends on how one responds to the opportunities of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Everything turns on how we respond to the opportunities of the moment.

sentences.zh: 望降臣章與二三大臣熟議之。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will circulate this minister's memorial for thorough discussion with your leading ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty circulate this memorial for thorough discussion among your chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 」詔：綱所陳，今日之急務，付三省、樞密院施行。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: What Gang has presented are today's urgent priorities; assign them to the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict responded that what Li Gang had presented were urgent priorities of the day and ordered the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 時韓世忠屢敗金人于淮、楚間，有旨督劉光世、張浚統兵渡河，車駕進發至江上勞軍。

translations.literal: At that time Han Shizhong had repeatedly defeated the Jurchens between the Huai and Chu regions. An edict ordered Liu Guangshi and Zhang Jun to lead troops across the river; the imperial carriage advanced to the Yangzi to review the troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Shizhong had repeatedly defeated the Jurchens between the Huai and Chu regions. An edict ordered Liu Guangshi and Zhang Jun to lead troops across the river, and the imperial carriage advanced to the Yangzi to review the army.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔問攻戰、守備、措置、綏懷之方，綱奏：

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict inquired about methods of attack, defense, arrangements, and pacification. Gang submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, an edict asked for plans on attack, defense, institutional arrangements, and pacification. Li Gang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿以敵退為可喜，而以仇敵未報為可憤；

translations.literal: May Your Majesty not rejoice that the enemy has withdrawn, but feel anger that your foe has not yet been avenged;
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty not rejoice that the enemy has withdrawn, but feel anger that your sworn foe remains unavenged;

sentences.zh: 勿以東南為可安，而以中原未復、赤縣神州陷於敵國為可恥；

translations.literal: not consider the southeast secure, but feel shame that the Central Plain is not recovered and the sacred land lies under an enemy state;
translations.idiomatic: not treat the southeast as secure, but feel shame that the Central Plain remains unrecovered and our sacred homeland lies under enemy rule;

sentences.zh: 勿以諸將屢捷為可賀，而以軍政未修、士氣未振而強敵猶得以潛逃為可虞。

translations.literal: not congratulate yourselves on the generals' repeated victories, but worry that military administration is not restored, morale is not revived, and a powerful enemy still slips away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: not congratulate yourselves on the generals' repeated victories, but worry that military administration remains unreformed, morale unrevived, and a powerful enemy still able to slip away unscathed.

sentences.zh: 則中興之期，可指日而俟。

translations.literal: Then the day of restoration can be awaited within counting distance.
translations.idiomatic: Then the day of national restoration would be close at hand.

sentences.zh: 議者或謂敵馬既退，當遂用兵為大舉之計，臣竊以為不然。

translations.literal: Some commentators say that since the enemy cavalry has withdrawn, we should immediately use troops for a major campaign. I privately think this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers argue that since the enemy cavalry has withdrawn, we should immediately launch a major military campaign. I respectfully disagree.

sentences.zh: 生理未固，而欲浪戰以僥倖，非制勝之術也。

translations.literal: When our livelihood is not yet secure, to seek reckless battle for a lucky break is not the art of achieving victory.
translations.idiomatic: When our foundations are not yet secure, to gamble on reckless battle is not the way to victory.

sentences.zh: 高祖先保關中，故能東向與項籍爭。

translations.literal: The Founder of Han first secured Guanzhong, and thus was able to turn east and contend with Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han first secured Guanzhong, and only then was able to turn east and contend with Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 光武先保河內，故能降赤眉、銅馬之屬。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu first secured Henei, and thus was able to subdue the Red Eyebrows, Bronze Horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu first secured Henei, and only then was able to subdue the Red Eyebrows, Bronze Horses, and their like.

sentences.zh: 肅宗先保靈武，故能破安、史而復兩京。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong first secured Lingwu, and thus was able to break An Lushan and Shi Siming and recover the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong first secured Lingwu, and only then was able to defeat An Lushan and Shi Siming and recover the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷以東南為根本，將士暴露之久，財用調度之煩，民力科取之困，苟不大修守備，痛自料理，先為自固之計，何以能萬全而制敵？

translations.literal: Now the court takes the southeast as its foundation. Officers and soldiers have long been exposed to the elements; finances are troublesome to allocate; the people's strength is strained by levies. If we do not greatly strengthen defenses and painstakingly put our house in order, first planning for self-consolidation—how can we be fully secure and overcome the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Today the court takes the southeast as its foundation. Officers and soldiers have long endured hardship in the field; finances are hard to manage; and the people are exhausted by levies. Unless we greatly strengthen our defenses and put our house in order first, how can we be secure and overcome the enemy?

sentences.zh: 議者又謂敵人既退，當且保據一隅，以苟目前之安，臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: Commentators also say that since the enemy has withdrawn, we should for now hold to one corner and scrape by for present security. I again think this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Others argue that since the enemy has withdrawn, we should simply hold one corner of the realm and settle for present security. I disagree with that as well.

sentences.zh: 秦師三伐晉，以報殽之師；

translations.literal: The troops of Qin thrice attacked Jin to avenge the defeat at Xiao;
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Qin attacked Jin three times to avenge the defeat at Xiao;

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮佐蜀，連年出師以圖中原，不如是，不足以立國。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang assisted Shu, sending out armies year after year to plan for the Central Plain. Without this, it would not suffice to establish the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang served Shu and sent armies out year after year to recover the Central Plain; without that, the state could not endure.

sentences.zh: 高祖在漢中，謂蕭何曰：'吾亦欲東。

translations.literal: The Founder in Hanzhong said to Xiao He: "I too wish to go east."
translations.idiomatic: While still in Hanzhong, Gaozu said to Xiao He, "I too mean to turn east."

sentences.zh: '光武破隗囂，既平隴，復望蜀。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu, having defeated Wei Xiao and pacified Long, again looked toward Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, after defeating Wei Xiao and pacifying Long, turned his gaze toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 此皆以天下為度，不如是，不足以混一區宇，戡定禍亂。

translations.literal: All measured the realm as a whole; without this, it would not suffice to unify the land and quell disorder.
translations.idiomatic: All of them measured affairs by the whole realm; without that outlook, one cannot unify the empire and quell chaos.

sentences.zh: 況祖宗境土，豈可坐視淪陷，不務恢復乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, the lands of our ancestors—how can we sit and watch them fall without striving for recovery?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for the lands of our ancestors—can we sit by and watch them fall without striving for recovery?

sentences.zh: 今歲不征，明年不戰，使敵勢益張，而吾之所糾合精銳士馬，日以損耗，何以圖敵？

translations.literal: If we do not campaign this year or fight next year, the enemy's power will only grow, while the elite troops and horses we have gathered will daily diminish—how then can we plan against the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If we neither campaign this year nor fight next, the enemy will grow stronger while the elite troops and horses we have assembled are worn down day by day—how then can we hope to defeat them?

sentences.zh: 謂宜於防守既固、軍政既修之後，即議攻討，乃為得計。

translations.literal: I say that once defenses are secure and military administration is restored, we should then deliberate on attack—that is the proper plan.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once defenses are secure and military administration restored, we should then discuss offensive action—that is the sound course.

sentences.zh: 此二者，守備、攻戰之序也。

translations.literal: These two are the sequence of defense and attack.
translations.idiomatic: These two points define the proper order of defense and attack.

sentences.zh: 至於守備之宜，則當科理淮南、荊襄，以為東南遮罩。

translations.literal: As for what is appropriate in defense, we should organize Huainan and Jing-Xiang as a protective screen for the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: As for proper defense, Huainan and Jing-Xiang should be organized as a protective screen for the southeast.

sentences.zh: 夫六朝之所以能保有江左者，以強兵巨鎮，盡在淮南、荊襄間。

translations.literal: The reason the Six Dynasties could hold the lands south of the Yangzi was that their strongest armies and greatest garrisons were all in the Huainan and Jing-Xiang regions.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the Six Dynasties were able to hold the lands south of the Yangzi was that their strongest armies and greatest garrisons lay in Huainan and Jing-Xiang.

sentences.zh: 故以魏武之雄，苻堅、石勒之眾，宇文、拓拔之盛，卒不能窺江表。

translations.literal: Thus despite Cao Cao's prowess, the multitudes of Fu Jian and Shi Le, and the might of the Yuwen and Tuoba—none in the end could gaze covetously upon the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even the prowess of Cao Cao, the vast hosts of Fu Jian and Shi Le, and the power of the Yuwen and Tuoba clans could not in the end threaten the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 後唐李氏有淮南，則可以都金陵，其後淮南為周世宗所取，遂以削弱。

translations.literal: When the Later Tang Li clan held Huainan, they could make Jinling their capital. Afterward Huainan was taken by Emperor Shizong of Zhou, and they were consequently weakened.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Tang Li house held Huainan, it could make Jinling its capital; once Huainan was taken by Emperor Shizong of Zhou, the dynasty was weakened.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，大將擁重兵于江南，官吏守空城於江北，雖有天險而無戰艦水軍之制，故敵人得以侵擾窺伺。

translations.literal: In recent years, great generals have hoarded heavy troops south of the Yangzi while officials hold empty cities north of the river. Though there are natural barriers, there is no system of warships and naval forces—hence the enemy has been able to harass and probe.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years great generals have hoarded heavy forces south of the Yangzi while officials hold empty cities north of the river. Though natural barriers exist, there is no proper system of warships and naval forces, so the enemy has been able to raid and probe at will.

sentences.zh: 今當於淮之東西及荊襄置三大帥，屯重兵以臨之，分遣偏師，進守支郡，加以戰艦水軍，上運下接，自為防守。

translations.literal: Now we should establish three supreme commanders east and west of the Huai and in Jing-Xiang, station heavy troops to face the enemy, dispatch detached columns to advance and hold subsidiary prefectures, add warships and naval forces linking upstream and downstream, and thus provide our own defense.
translations.idiomatic: We should now appoint three supreme commanders east and west of the Huai and in Jing-Xiang, station heavy forces to face the enemy, dispatch detached columns to hold subsidiary prefectures, and build a linked system of warships and naval forces upstream and downstream to defend ourselves.

sentences.zh: 敵馬雖多，不敢輕犯，則藩籬之勢盛而無窮之利也。

translations.literal: Though enemy cavalry is numerous, they will not dare lightly transgress—then the strength of our outer defenses will flourish, with endless benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Even if enemy cavalry is numerous, it will not dare lightly attack, and the strength of our outer defenses will grow with lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 有守備矣，然後議攻戰之利，分責諸路，因利乘便，收復京畿，以及故都。

translations.literal: Once there is defense, then discuss the benefits of attack—assign responsibility to each route, seize advantage and opportunity, recover the capital region and the former capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once defenses are in place, we can then discuss the gains of offensive action, assign responsibility to each route, seize opportunities as they arise, and recover the capital region and the former capital.

sentences.zh: 斷以必為之志而勿失機會，則以弱為強，取威定亂於一勝之間，逆臣可誅，強敵可滅，攻戰之利，莫大於是。

translations.literal: With resolute will and without missing opportunity, we transform weakness into strength, establishing authority and quelling chaos in a single victory—rebellious ministers can be executed, powerful enemies can be destroyed. No benefit of attack is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: With resolute purpose and without missing the moment, weakness can be turned into strength, authority established and chaos settled in a single victory—traitors can be punished and powerful enemies destroyed. No gain from offensive action is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 若夫萬乘所居，必擇形勝以為駐蹕之所，然後能制服中外，以圖事業。

translations.literal: As for where the Son of Heaven dwells, one must choose commanding terrain as the place to halt the imperial progress, and only then can one control within and without to pursue great undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: As for where the Son of Heaven resides, he must choose commanding terrain as the place to halt the imperial progress; only then can he control the realm within and without and pursue great undertakings.

sentences.zh: 建康自昔號帝王之宅，江山雄壯，地勢寬博，六朝更都之。

translations.literal: Jianye has from ancient times been called the abode of emperors—its rivers and mountains are majestic, its terrain broad. The Six Dynasties in succession made it their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye has long been called the abode of emperors; its rivers and mountains are majestic and its terrain broad, and the Six Dynasties in succession made it their capital.

sentences.zh: 臣昔舉天下形勢而言，謂關中為上，今以東南形勢而言，則當以建康為便。

translations.literal: Your minister once spoke of the realm's strategic geography and said Guanzhong was supreme. Speaking now of the southeast's strategic geography, Jianye should be preferred.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister once surveyed the strategic geography of the whole realm and ranked Guanzhong first; speaking now of the southeast alone, Jianye is the better choice.

sentences.zh: 今者，鑾輿未復舊都，莫若且于建康權宜駐蹕。

translations.literal: At present the imperial carriage has not returned to the old capital. It would be best to halt temporarily at Jianye as an expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial carriage has not yet returned to the old capital, it would be best to halt temporarily at Jianye as an expedient measure.

sentences.zh: 願詔守臣治城池，修宮闕，立官府，創營壁，使粗成規模，以待巡幸。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the defending officials to repair walls and moats, restore palaces and halls, establish government offices, and build fortifications, so that a rough framework is formed in readiness for an imperial visit.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the local officials to repair walls and moats, restore palaces and halls, establish government offices, and build fortifications until a basic framework is ready for an imperial visit.

sentences.zh: 蓋有城池然後人心不恐，有官府然後政事可修，有營壘然後士卒可用，此措置之所當先也。

translations.literal: For only with city walls will the people's hearts not fear; only with government offices can administration be maintained; only with fortifications can soldiers be deployed. This is what arrangements must prioritize.
translations.idiomatic: Only with city walls will the people cease to fear; only with government offices can administration function; only with fortifications can soldiers be deployed. These are the arrangements that must come first.

sentences.zh: 至於西北之民，皆陛下赤子，荷祖宗涵養之深，其心未嘗一日忘宋。

translations.literal: As for the people of the northwest—all are Your Majesty's own children. Having received the deep nurture of our ancestors, their hearts have never for a day forgotten Song.
translations.idiomatic: As for the people of the northwest, all are Your Majesty's own children. Nurtured deeply by our ancestors, their hearts have never for a day forgotten Song.

sentences.zh: 特製於強敵，陷於塗炭，而不能以自歸。

translations.literal: They are only constrained by a powerful enemy, sunk in misery, and unable to return on their own.
translations.idiomatic: They are only held back by a powerful enemy, sunk in misery, and unable to return on their own.

sentences.zh: 天威震驚，必有結納來歸、願為內應者。

translations.literal: When imperial majesty strikes terror, there will surely be those who forge ties, come over, and wish to serve as internal allies.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial majesty strikes terror, there will surely be those who forge ties, come over, and offer to serve as internal allies.

sentences.zh: 宜給之土田，予以爵賞，優加撫循，許其自新，使陷溺之民知所依怙，莫不感悅，益堅戴宋之心，此綏懷之所當先也。

translations.literal: We should grant them land, bestow ranks and rewards, treat them with special care, permit their renewal, so that people sunk in peril know whom to rely upon—all will be moved with joy and further strengthen their loyalty to Song. This is what pacification must prioritize.
translations.idiomatic: They should be granted land, given ranks and rewards, treated with special care, and allowed to start anew, so that people sunk in misery know whom to rely on, all are moved to gratitude, and loyalty to Song is strengthened. This is what pacification must prioritize.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀陛下有聰明睿智之姿，有英武敢為之志，然自臨禦，迨今九年，國不辟而日蹙，事不立而日壞，將驕而難禦，卒惰而未練，國用匱而無贏餘之蓄，民力困而無休息之期。

translations.literal: Your minister privately observes that Your Majesty has a brilliant and discerning nature and a bold and resolute will—yet since ascending the throne, now nine years on, the realm has not expanded but daily contracts; affairs are not established but daily worsen; generals are proud and hard to control; soldiers are lax and untrained; state finances are depleted with no surplus stored; the people's strength is exhausted with no rest in sight.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister privately observes that Your Majesty possesses a brilliant and discerning mind and a bold, resolute will, yet in the nine years since ascending the throne the realm has not expanded but daily contracts; affairs are not established but daily worsen; generals are arrogant and hard to control; soldiers are lax and untrained; state finances are depleted with no surplus in store; and the people are exhausted with no respite in sight.

sentences.zh: 使陛下憂勤雖至，而中興之效，邈乎無聞，則群臣誤陛下之故也。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty's worry and diligence reach their utmost, yet the fruits of restoration are nowhere heard of—it is because your ministers have misled Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty's worry and diligence have been extreme, the fruits of restoration are nowhere to be seen—it is because your ministers have misled you.

sentences.zh: 陛下觀近年以來所用之臣，慨然敢以天下之重自任者幾人？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, look at the ministers employed in recent years—how many can you say have boldly taken upon themselves the weight of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, look at the ministers employed in recent years—how many have truly dared to take the weight of the realm upon themselves?

sentences.zh: 平居無事，小廉曲謹，似可無過，忽有擾攘，則錯愕無所措手足，不過奉身以退，天下憂危之重，委之陛下而已。

translations.literal: In peace they seem faultless with petty integrity and narrow caution. When sudden turmoil arises, they are bewildered and at a loss, doing nothing but protecting themselves and withdrawing—the weight of the realm's peril they leave entirely to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: In peaceful times they appear scrupulous and faultless; when sudden crisis erupts, they are bewildered and helpless, doing nothing but protect themselves and withdraw, leaving the weight of the realm's peril entirely to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 有臣如此，不知何補于國，而陛下亦安取此？

translations.literal: With ministers such as these, what use are they to the state? And why should Your Majesty employ them?
translations.idiomatic: With ministers such as these, what good are they to the state? And why should Your Majesty keep them?

sentences.zh: 夫用人如用醫，必先知其術業可以已病，乃可使之進藥而責成功。

translations.literal: Employing men is like employing physicians: one must first know their skill can cure the illness before entrusting them with medicine and demanding success.
translations.idiomatic: Employing men is like employing physicians: one must first know that their skill can cure the disease before entrusting them with medicine and demanding success.

sentences.zh: 今不詳審其術業而姑試之，則雖日易一醫，無補於病，徒加疾而已。

translations.literal: Now, without carefully examining their skill, one merely tries them in turn—then though one changes physicians daily, it does no good for the illness but only worsens the malady.
translations.idiomatic: If their skill is not carefully examined and they are simply tried one after another, then even changing physicians every day will not cure the illness but only make it worse.

sentences.zh: 大概近年，閒暇則以和議為得計，而以治兵為失策，倉卒則以退避為愛君，而以進禦為誤國。

translations.literal: In general, in recent years: in leisure, peace talks are considered wise and training troops foolish; in crisis, retreat is considered loving the ruler and advancing to defend considered betraying the state.
translations.idiomatic: In general, in recent years peace talks have been treated as wise policy in quiet times and military preparation as folly; in crisis, retreat has been treated as loyalty to the ruler and advancing to defend as betrayal of the state.

sentences.zh: 上下偷安，不為長久之計。

translations.literal: Above and below seek ease for themselves, making no long-term plans.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below seek their own ease and make no long-term plans.

sentences.zh: 天步艱難，國勢益弱，職此之由。

translations.literal: Heaven's course is arduous; the realm grows weaker—this is the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course has grown arduous and the realm ever weaker—this is why.

sentences.zh: 今天啟宸衷，悟前日和議退避之失，親臨大敵。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has opened Your Majesty's heart; you have perceived the errors of earlier peace talks and retreat, and personally faced the great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has opened Your Majesty's heart; you have seen the errors of earlier peace talks and retreat, and personally faced the great enemy.

sentences.zh: 天威所臨，使北軍數十萬之眾，震怖不敢南渡，潛師宵奔。

translations.literal: Where imperial majesty presided, several hundred thousand northern troops trembled in terror and dared not cross south; their hidden forces fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Where imperial majesty presided, several hundred thousand northern troops trembled in terror and dared not cross south, and their hidden forces fled by night.

sentences.zh: 則和議之與治兵，退避之與進禦，其效概可睹矣。

translations.literal: Then the effects of peace talks versus training troops, retreat versus advancing to defend, can broadly be seen.
translations.idiomatic: The contrast between peace talks and military preparation, between retreat and advancing to defend, can now be seen plainly.

sentences.zh: 然敵兵雖退，未大懲創，安知其秋高馬肥，不再來擾我疆埸，使疲於奔命哉？

translations.literal: Yet though the enemy has withdrawn, they have not been greatly punished. Who knows whether, when autumn is high and horses are fat, they will not again come to trouble our borders and wear us down with constant alarms?
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the enemy has withdrawn, it has not been severely punished. Who knows whether, when autumn comes and horses grow fat, it will not return to trouble our borders and wear us down with constant alarms?

sentences.zh: 若夫退避之策，可暫而不可常，可一而不可再，退一步則失一步，退一尺則失一尺。

translations.literal: As for the strategy of retreat—it may be used temporarily but not permanently, once but not twice. One step back loses one step; one foot back loses one foot.
translations.idiomatic: As for the strategy of retreat, it may be used temporarily but not permanently, once but not twice: one step back loses one step, one foot back loses one foot.

sentences.zh: 往時自南都退而至維揚，則關陝、河北、河東失矣；

translations.literal: In past times, retreating from the Southern Capital to Weiyang meant losing Guan-Shaan, Hebei, and Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: In the past, retreat from the Southern Capital to Weiyang meant the loss of Guan-Shaan, Hebei, and Hedong;

sentences.zh: 自維揚退而至江、浙，則京東、西失矣。

translations.literal: retreating from Weiyang to Jiang and Zhe meant losing the eastern and western capital regions.
translations.idiomatic: retreat from Weiyang to Jiang and Zhe meant the loss of the eastern and western capital regions.

sentences.zh: 萬有一敵騎南牧，復將退避。

translations.literal: If by any chance enemy cavalry again drive south, are we once more to retreat?
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance enemy cavalry again drive south, are we to retreat once more?

sentences.zh: 不知何所適而可乎？

translations.literal: To where can we go that would be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Where could we go that would be acceptable?

sentences.zh: 航海之策，萬乘冒風濤不測之險，此又不可之尤者也。

translations.literal: The strategy of taking to the sea—having the Son of Heaven brave the unpredictable dangers of wind and waves—this above all is what must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy of taking to the sea, exposing the Son of Heaven to the unpredictable dangers of wind and waves, is above all what must not be done.

sentences.zh: 惟當于國家閒暇之時，明政刑，治軍旅，選將帥，修車馬，備器械，峙糗糧，積金帛。

translations.literal: We should only, in the nation's intervals of peace, clarify laws and punishments, discipline the army, select generals, maintain chariots and horses, prepare weapons, stockpile provisions, and accumulate gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: We should use the nation's intervals of peace to clarify laws and punishments, discipline the army, select generals, maintain chariots and horses, prepare weapons, stockpile provisions, and accumulate gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 敵來則禦，俟時而奮，以光復祖宗之大業，此最上策也。

translations.literal: When the enemy comes, defend; wait for the moment to strike—to restore the great enterprise of our ancestors. This is the supreme strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy comes, defend; when the moment arrives, strike—to restore the great enterprise of our ancestors. That is the supreme strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下自今以往，勿復為退避之計，可乎？

translations.literal: Your minister humbly hopes that from this day forward Your Majesty will no longer resort to plans of retreat—is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Your minister humbly asks that from this day forward Your Majesty will no longer resort to plans of retreat—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 臣又觀古者敵國善鄰，則有和親，仇讎之邦，鮮復遣使。

translations.literal: Your minister further observes that in antiquity, when neighboring states were friendly, there was marriage alliance; between sworn enemies, envoys were rarely sent.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister further observes that in antiquity friendly neighboring states exchanged marriage alliances, while sworn enemies rarely sent envoys to one another.

sentences.zh: 豈不以釁隙既深，終無講好修睦之理故耶？

translations.literal: Is this not because enmity runs so deep that reconciliation and neighborly harmony are ultimately impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because once enmity runs so deep, there is ultimately no basis for peace and good relations?

sentences.zh: 東晉渡江，石勒遣使于晉，元帝命焚其幣而卻其使。

translations.literal: When Eastern Jin crossed the Yangzi, Shi Le sent envoys to Jin; Emperor Yuan ordered the gifts burned and the envoys rejected.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Jin crossed the Yangzi, Shi Le sent envoys to Jin, and Emperor Yuan ordered the gifts burned and the envoys turned away.

sentences.zh: 彼遣使來，且猶卻之，此何可往？

translations.literal: When they sent envoys, those were still rejected—how then can we go to them?
translations.idiomatic: When they came as envoys, they were still turned away—how then can we go to them?

sentences.zh: 假道僭偽之國，其自取辱，無補於事，祗傷國體。

translations.literal: Passing through a usurping false state—we invite humiliation ourselves, accomplish nothing, and only injure the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: To pass through a usurping puppet state is to invite humiliation, accomplish nothing, and only injure the dignity of the realm.

sentences.zh: 金人造釁之深，知我必報，其措意為何如？

translations.literal: The Jurchens' provocation runs deep; they know we must retaliate—what do they intend?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens' provocation runs deep; they know we must retaliate—what then do they intend?

sentences.zh: 而我方且卑辭厚幣，屈體以求之，其不推誠以見信，決矣。

translations.literal: Yet we demean ourselves with humble words and rich gifts, bowing our bodies to seek peace—they will assuredly not treat us with sincerity or trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we demean ourselves with humble words and rich gifts, bowing low to seek peace—they will assuredly not treat us with sincerity or trust.

sentences.zh: 器幣禮物，所費不貲，使軺往來，坐索士氣，而又邀我以必不可從之事，制我以必不敢為之謀，是和卒不成，而徒為此擾擾也。

translations.literal: Vessels, silks, and gifts cost incalculable sums; envoys shuttle back and forth, draining morale; and they impose on us what we absolutely cannot agree to, constraining us from plans we must dare not make—peace in the end will not be achieved, and all this bustle is for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels, silks, and gifts cost incalculable sums; envoys shuttle back and forth, draining morale; and they impose terms we cannot accept and constrain plans we dare not pursue—peace will never be achieved, and all this bustle is for nothing.

sentences.zh: 非特如此，于吾自治自強之計，動輒相妨，實有所害。

translations.literal: Not only this—it actively obstructs our plans for self-governance and self-strengthening and truly does harm.
translations.idiomatic: Not only that—it constantly obstructs our plans for self-governance and self-strengthening and truly does harm.

sentences.zh: 金人二十餘年，以此策破契丹、困中國，而終莫之悟。

translations.literal: For over twenty years the Jurchens have used this strategy to break the Khitans and trap China—and we have never awakened to it.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years the Jurchens have used this strategy to break the Khitans and trap China, and we have never awakened to it.

sentences.zh: 夫辨是非利害者，人心所同，豈真不悟哉？

translations.literal: Discerning right from wrong and benefit from harm is what all hearts share—are we truly unaware?
translations.idiomatic: Discerning right from wrong and benefit from harm is common to all hearts—are we truly unaware?

sentences.zh: 聊復用此以僥倖萬一，曾不知為吾害者甚大，此古人所謂幾何僥倖而不喪人之國者也。

translations.literal: We simply employ it again hoping for one chance in ten thousand, never realizing how greatly it harms us—this is what the ancients called: how much luck before one loses one's kingdom?
translations.idiomatic: We simply employ it again hoping for one chance in ten thousand, never realizing how greatly it harms us—this is what the ancients meant by gambling on luck until one loses one's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 臣願自今以往，勿復遣和議之使，可乎？

translations.literal: Your minister humbly hopes that from this day forward no peace envoys will be sent—is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Your minister humbly asks that from this day forward no peace envoys be sent—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 二說既定，擇所當為者，一切以至誠為之。

translations.literal: Once these two positions are settled, choose what ought to be done and pursue it all with utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Once these two positions are settled, choose what ought to be done and pursue it with utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 俟吾之政事修，倉廩實，府庫充，器用備，士氣振，力可有為，乃議大舉，則兵雖未交，而勝負之勢已決矣。

translations.literal: Wait until our administration is restored, granaries filled, treasuries stocked, weapons prepared, and morale revived—when our strength permits action—then deliberate on a major campaign. Though armies have not yet clashed, the trend of victory and defeat will already be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until administration is restored, granaries filled, treasuries stocked, weapons prepared, and morale revived—when our strength permits action—then deliberate on a major campaign. Though armies have not yet clashed, the outcome will already be decided.

sentences.zh: 抑臣聞朝廷者根本也，藩方者枝葉也，根本固則枝葉蕃，朝廷者腹心也，將士者爪牙也，腹心壯則爪牙奮。

translations.literal: Moreover, your minister has heard: the court is the root, the provinces the branches and leaves—when the root is firm, the branches flourish. The court is the heart and belly, the officers and soldiers the claws and fangs—when the heart is strong, the claws and fangs strike fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your minister has heard that the court is the root and the provinces the branches and leaves—when the root is firm, the branches flourish; the court is the heart and the officers and soldiers the claws and fangs—when the heart is strong, the claws and fangs strike fiercely.

sentences.zh: 今遠而強敵，近而偽臣，國家所仰以為捍蔽者在藩方，所資以致攻討者在將士，然根本腹心則在朝廷。

translations.literal: Now with a strong enemy far away and a false minister nearby, what the state relies on for defense and shielding is in the frontier regions, what it draws on for attack and campaigns is in its generals and soldiers, yet the root and vital core lie in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Though our formidable foe lies far away and a puppet regime lurks close at hand, the regions upon which the state depends for defense are on the frontiers, and the generals and troops on whom we rely for offensive campaigns are in the field — yet the root and heart of all this lie in the imperial court itself.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下正心以正朝廷百官，使君子小人各得其分，則是非明，賞罰當，自然藩方協力，將士用命，雖強敵不足畏，逆臣不足憂，此特在陛下方寸之間耳。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty corrects your heart to set right the court and all officials, so that the noble and the base each obtain their proper place, then right and wrong will be clear, rewards and punishments will be fitting, naturally the frontier regions will cooperate, generals and soldiers will obey commands — even a strong enemy need not be feared, a rebellious minister need not be worried about. This rests entirely within Your Majesty's own breast.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would only set your own heart right to set the court and all officials right — letting the upright and the corrupt each keep to their proper place — right and wrong would be clear, rewards and punishments would be just, the frontier regions would naturally pull together, and troops would follow orders willingly. Then even a mighty enemy would hold no terror, and even traitors would merit no anxiety. All of this rests within the compass of Your Majesty's own mind.

sentences.zh: 臣昧死上條六事：一曰信任輔弼，二曰公選人材，三曰變革士風，四曰愛惜日力，五曰務盡人事，六曰寅畏天威。

translations.literal: Your subject, risking death, submits these six items: first, trust your chief ministers; second, select talent impartially; third, reform the character of scholars; fourth, cherish each day's effort; fifth, exert all human effort; sixth, revere Heaven's majesty in fear.
translations.idiomatic: At the risk of my life, your servant submits six recommendations: first, trust your chief ministers; second, select talent impartially; third, reform the prevailing character of the scholar-official class; fourth, cherish and make good use of time; fifth, exert every possible human effort; sixth, stand in reverent awe of Heaven's authority.

sentences.zh: 何謂信任輔弼？

translations.literal: What is meant by trusting chief ministers?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to trust one's chief ministers?

sentences.zh: 夫興衰撥亂之主，必有同心同德之臣相與有為，如元首股肱之于一身，父子兄弟之于一家，乃能協濟。

translations.literal: Now, rulers who raise up what is declining or put chaos in order must have ministers of one heart and one virtue working together with them, like head and limbs to a single body, like father and sons and brothers to one household — only then can they achieve mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who would reverse decline or restore order from chaos must have ministers of one heart and one purpose working with him — like head and limbs to a single body, like father, sons, and brothers within one household — before such cooperation can succeed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下選于眾以圖任，遂能捍禦大敵，可謂得人矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has chosen from the multitude for strategic appointments, and thus been able to repel a great enemy — this may be called obtaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has chosen the right men from among many for the great tasks of state, and so has been able to repel a formidable enemy — this truly counts as finding the right people.

sentences.zh: 然臣願陛下待以至誠，無事形跡，久任以責成功，勿使小人得以間之，則君臣之美，垂於無窮矣。

translations.literal: Yet your subject wishes Your Majesty to treat them with utmost sincerity, without scrutinizing outward signs, entrust them for long terms and hold them responsible for results, and not let petty men sow division between you — then the beauty of ruler and minister will extend to endless generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I pray Your Majesty will treat them with complete sincerity, without picking at outward signs of loyalty, keep them in office long enough to demand real results, and not let petty men drive wedges between you — then the excellence of the bond between sovereign and minister will endure without end.

sentences.zh: 何謂公選人才？

translations.literal: What is meant by impartial selection of talent?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to select talent impartially?

sentences.zh: 夫治天下者，必資于人才，而創業、中興之主，所資尤多。

translations.literal: One who governs All Under Heaven must rely on talent; yet founders and restorers of dynasties rely on talent above all.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the realm one must rely on talent — but founders and restorers of dynasties rely on it above all else.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 繼體守文，率由舊章，得中庸之才，亦足以共治；

translations.literal: In inheriting the throne and maintaining established institutions, following old precedents, even men of middling talent are sufficient to govern together.
translations.idiomatic: When one succeeds to the throne and preserves existing institutions, following established precedent, even men of ordinary ability may suffice to share in governance.

sentences.zh: 至於艱難之際，非得卓犖瑰偉之才，則未易有濟。

translations.literal: But in times of hardship, unless one obtains extraordinary and magnificent talent, success is not easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In times of hardship, however, without truly exceptional talent, success is hard to attain.

sentences.zh: 是以大有為之主，必有不世出之才，參贊翊佐，以成大業。

translations.literal: Therefore a ruler intent on great achievement must have once-in-a-generation talent to assist and support him in completing the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Hence a ruler who would accomplish great things must have rare, unequaled talent to assist and advise him if the great enterprise is to succeed.

sentences.zh: 然自昔抱不群之才者，多為小人之所忌嫉，或中之以黯暗，或指之為黨與，或誣之以大惡，或擿之以細故。

translations.literal: Yet from of old, those who possessed uncommon talent were mostly envied by petty men — some were struck with vague insinuations, some labeled as faction members, some slandered with grave crimes, some pounced upon for trivial faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from ancient times, men who possessed exceptional talent have often been envied by the petty-minded — assailed with dark insinuations, denounced as partisans, falsely charged with grave crimes, or trapped over trifling offenses.

sentences.zh: 而以道事君者，不可則止，難於自進，恥於自明，雖負重謗、遭深譴，安於義命，不復自辨。

translations.literal: But those who serve their ruler according to the Way, when not accepted stop; they find it hard to press their case, shameful to plead their own innocence. Though bearing heavy slander and suffering deep punishment, they rest content with right and fate and do not argue further for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who serve their sovereign according to the Way, when rebuffed, simply withdraw; they find it hard to push themselves forward and shameful to plead their own case. Though burdened with heavy slander and deep punishment, they are content with what duty and fate require and do not defend themselves further.

sentences.zh: 苟非至明之主，深察人之情偽，安能辨其非辜哉？

translations.literal: If not a supremely discerning ruler who deeply observes the truth and falsity in men's hearts, how could one distinguish their innocence?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the ruler is supremely wise and sees clearly through men's truth and pretense, how can innocent men be distinguished from the guilty?

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦以來，用人多矣，世之所許以為端人正士者，往往閑廢於無用之地；

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have employed many men — yet those the world acknowledges as upright and principled are often left idle in places where they can do no good.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, many men have been appointed — yet those the world acknowledges as upright and principled are often cast aside in positions where they can do no good.

sentences.zh: 而陛下寤寐側席，有乏材之歎，盍少留意而致察焉！

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty, unable to sleep for worry, sits upright on your bed, sighing over the lack of talent — why not pay some attention and investigate?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Your Majesty tosses sleeplessly on your bed, lamenting the lack of talent — why not look more closely and investigate?

sentences.zh: 何謂變革士風？

translations.literal: What is meant by reforming the character of scholars?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to reform the prevailing character of the scholar-official class?

sentences.zh: 夫用兵之與士風，似不相及，而實相為表裏。

translations.literal: Now the use of troops and the character of scholars seem unrelated, yet in fact they are inner and outer to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The use of armies and the character of the scholar-official class may seem unrelated, yet in truth they are the inner and outer of the same thing.

sentences.zh: 士風厚則議正而是非明，朝廷賞罰當功罪而人心服，考之本朝嘉祐、治平以前可知已。

translations.literal: When the character of scholars is solid, deliberations are upright and right and wrong are clear; the court's rewards and punishments fit merit and fault and men's hearts submit — examining our dynasty before the Jiayou and Zhiping eras proves this.
translations.idiomatic: When the moral tone of the scholar-official class is strong, debate is upright, right and wrong are clear, and when the court's rewards and punishments fit merit and fault, the people accept them — as can be seen from our own dynasty before the Jiayou and Zhiping reign periods.

sentences.zh: 數十年來，奔競日進，論議徇私，邪說利口，足以惑人主之聽。

translations.literal: For several decades, scrambling for advancement has grown daily; deliberations have been partial to private interest; wicked doctrines and glib tongues have been enough to confuse the ruler's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: For decades advancement has grown ever more frantic, debate ever more self-serving, and perverse doctrines and glib tongues have been enough to cloud the sovereign's judgment.

sentences.zh: 元祐大臣，持正論如司馬光之流，皆社稷之臣也，而群枉嫉之，指為奸黨，顛倒是非，政事大壞，馴致靖康之變，非偶然也。

translations.literal: The Yuanyou ministers — men who upheld correct principles like Sima Guang — were all pillars of the state, yet the multitude of the crooked envied them, labeled them a wicked faction, inverted right and wrong, and government affairs were greatly ruined, gradually bringing on the disaster of Jingkang — this was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanyou ministers — upright men like Sima Guang who defended sound principle — were all pillars of the state, yet the corrupt envied them, denounced them as a wicked faction, inverted right and wrong, and ruined governance until the Jingkang catastrophe came — hardly by accident.

sentences.zh: 竊觀近年士風尤薄，隨時好惡，以取世資，潝訿成風，豈朝廷之福哉？

translations.literal: Your subject privately observes that in recent years the character of scholars has grown especially thin — shifting with the times, following likes and dislikes to obtain worldly gain, clamor and slander have become the fashion — is this a blessing for the court?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the moral tone of scholars has grown especially thin — men shift with the fashion, swayed by factional favor and disfavor to win worldly gain, until clamor and slander have become the norm. What blessing is this for the court?

sentences.zh: 大抵朝廷設耳目及獻納論思之官，固許之以風聞，至於大故，必須核實而後言。

translations.literal: Generally the court establishes censorial offices and posts for remonstrance and deliberation — rumor may indeed be permitted to them — but on major matters one must verify facts before speaking.
translations.idiomatic: In general the court maintains censorial and remonstrance offices that may indeed act on hearsay — but on serious matters they must verify the facts before speaking out.

sentences.zh: 使其無實，則誣人之罪，服讒搜慝，得以中害善良，皆非所以修政也。

translations.literal: If there is no substance, then the crime of false accusation, swallowing slander and hunting out the malicious, can succeed in striking down the good — none of this is the way to improve government.
translations.idiomatic: Where no substance exists, false accusation, credulous acceptance of slander, and the hunting out of the innocent can destroy good men — none of which serves to improve governance.

sentences.zh: 何謂愛惜日力？

translations.literal: What is meant by cherishing each day's effort?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to cherish and make good use of time?

sentences.zh: 夫創業、中興，如建大廈，堂室奧序，其規模可一日而成，鳩工聚材，則積累非一日所致。

translations.literal: Founding and restoration are like raising a great hall — the plan for halls, chambers, and inner rooms may be settled in a day, but gathering labor and material cannot be achieved in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Founding a dynasty and restoring it are like erecting a great mansion: the layout of halls and chambers may be settled in a day, but amassing labor and materials requires long accumulation.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦，九年於茲，境土未復，僭逆未誅，仇敵未報，尚稽中興之業者，誠以始不為之規模，而後不為之積累故也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled now for nine years — territory not yet recovered, the usurper not yet punished, the enemy not yet avenged, the work of restoration still delayed — truly because at the start no plan was made, and afterward no accumulation was built.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned for nine years, yet territory remains unreclaimed, the usurper unpunished, and the enemy unavenged, and the work of restoration still stalls — truly because at the outset no plan was laid, and afterward no foundations were steadily built.

sentences.zh: 邊事粗定之時，朝廷所推行者，不過簿書期會不切之細務，至於攻討防守之策，國之大計，皆未嘗留意。

translations.literal: When frontier affairs were roughly settled, what the court pursued was nothing but trivial business of ledgers and deadlines unrelated to essentials; as for strategies of attack, defense, and the great plans of state, none received attention.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier was somewhat calm, the court occupied itself only with petty paperwork and deadlines unrelated to essentials, while strategies of attack and defense and the state's great plans received no attention at all.

sentences.zh: 夫天下無不可為之事，亦無不可為之時。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there is nothing that cannot be done, and no time when things cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven there is nothing that cannot be done, and no time when it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 惟失其時，則事之小者日益大，事之易者日益難矣。

translations.literal: Only when the moment is missed do small matters daily grow larger and easy matters daily grow harder.
translations.idiomatic: Miss the right moment, and small problems grow larger day by day while easy tasks grow harder.

sentences.zh: 何謂務盡人事？

translations.literal: What is meant by exerting all human effort?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to exert every possible human effort?

sentences.zh: 夫天人之道，其實一致，人之所為，即天之所為也。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven and man is in fact one; what men do is what Heaven does.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven and the way of man are in truth one: what men do is what Heaven does.

sentences.zh: 人事盡於前，則天理應於後，此自然之符也。

translations.literal: When human effort is fully exerted first, Heaven's principle responds afterward — this is the natural correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: When human effort has been fully spent first, Heaven's will responds afterward — such is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 故創業、中興之主，盡其在我而已，其成功歸之於天。

translations.literal: Therefore founders and restorers exert all that lies within themselves, and attribute success to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Founders and restorers therefore do all that lies within their power, and only then ascribe success to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今未嘗盡人事，敵至而先自退屈，而欲責功於天，其可乎？

translations.literal: Now without having exerted all human effort, when the enemy comes you first retreat and yield of yourself, yet wish to assign merit to Heaven — is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, without having done all that human effort requires, you retreat before the enemy and then wish to assign the blame to Heaven — how can this be right?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下詔二三大臣，協心同力，盡人事以聽天命，則恢復土宇，剪屠鯨鯢，迎還兩宮，必有日矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to command the chief ministers to join hearts and combine strength, exert all human effort and then await Heaven's decree — then recovering territory, cutting down whales and crocodiles, and welcoming back the two palaces will surely come to pass in time.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will summon your chief ministers to join hearts and combine strength, do all that human effort allows and then await Heaven's mandate — then the recovery of our lands, the destruction of our monstrous foes, and the return of the Two Sovereigns will surely come in time.

sentences.zh: 何謂寅畏天威？

translations.literal: What is meant by reverently fearing Heaven's majesty?
translations.idiomatic: What does it mean to stand in reverent awe of Heaven's authority?

sentences.zh: 夫天之于王者，猶父母之于子，愛之至，則所以為之戒者亦至。

translations.literal: Heaven toward a king is like parents toward a child — when love reaches its height, so too do the warnings given.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's relation to a king is like that of parents to a child: the greater the love, the greater the warnings.

sentences.zh: 故人主之于天戒，必恐懼修省，以致其寅畏之誠。

translations.literal: Therefore toward Heaven's warnings a ruler must feel fear, cultivate himself, and thereby achieve sincere reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who receives Heaven's warnings must respond with fear and self-examination, so as to show sincere reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，熒惑失次，太白晝見，地震水溢，或久陰不雨，或久雨不霽，或當暑而寒，乃正月之朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In recent years Mars has left its station, Venus has appeared by day, the earth has quaked and waters overflowed — sometimes long clouds without rain, sometimes long rain without clearing, sometimes cold in what should be summer heat — and on the first day of the first month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Mars has strayed from its course, Venus has shone by day, the earth has shaken and waters have flooded — at times clouds linger without rain, at times rain pours without clearing, at times cold comes in midsummer — and on the first day of the first month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 此皆天意眷佑陛下，丁甯反覆，以致告戒。

translations.literal: All these are Heaven's care and protection for Your Majesty — repeated earnest admonitions to serve as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: All of these are Heaven's care for Your Majesty — repeated, earnest warnings.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下推至誠之意，正厥事以應之，則變災而為祥矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty extends utmost sincerity and sets right affairs in response, then disasters will turn to blessings.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty responds with utmost sincerity and sets affairs right, disaster will turn to blessing.

sentences.zh: 凡此六者，皆中興之業所關，而陛下所當先務者。

translations.literal: All these six items bear on the work of restoration, and are what Your Majesty should make priority matters.
translations.idiomatic: All six of these bear directly on the work of restoration, and are what Your Majesty should address first.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷人才不乏，將士足用，財用有餘，足為中興之資。

translations.literal: Now the court does not lack talent, generals and soldiers are sufficient, resources are ample — enough to serve as capital for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The court now lacks neither talent nor troops, and resources are sufficient — more than enough to fuel a restoration.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋鼎盛，欲大有為，何施不可？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's prime is in full vigor; if you wish to accomplish great things, what could not be done?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and wishes to accomplish great things — what could not be achieved?

sentences.zh: 要在改前日之轍，斷而行之耳。

translations.literal: The key is to change the track of former days and resolutely carry through — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The essential thing is to break from the errors of the past and resolutely follow through.

sentences.zh: 昔唐太宗謂魏征為敢言，征謝曰：「陛下導臣使言，不然，其敢批逆鱗哉。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang called Wei Zheng bold in speech. Wei Zheng thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty guided your subject to speak — otherwise, how would he dare touch the forbidden scales?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Taizong of Tang praised Wei Zheng for his bluntness. Wei Zheng replied: "Your Majesty encouraged me to speak — otherwise, how would I dare touch the dragon's scales?"

sentences.zh: 」今臣無魏征之敢言，然展盡底蘊，亦思慮之極也。

translations.literal: Now your subject lacks Wei Zheng's boldness in speech, yet in laying bare all within, this too is the utmost of deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant lacks Wei Zheng's boldness, yet in laying everything bare I have given all the thought I can.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下赦其愚直，而取其拳拳之忠。

translations.literal: Only pray Your Majesty pardon this dull straightforwardness and accept this earnest loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I pray only that Your Majesty will pardon my blunt foolishness and accept my earnest loyalty.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，上為賜詔褒諭。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor issued an edict commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor issued an edict praising and instructing him.

sentences.zh: 除江西安撫制置大使兼知洪州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Military Affairs of Jiangxi, concurrently Governor of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Military Affairs of Jiangxi, with concurrent duty as prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 有旨，赴行在奏事畢之官。

translations.literal: There was an edict that he should report at the mobile court and then proceed to his post upon finishing his audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to report to the mobile court and take up his post after presenting his business.

sentences.zh: 六年，綱至，引對內殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Gang arrived and was granted audience in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Li Gang arrived and was granted a private audience in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方銳意大舉，綱陛辭，言今日用兵之失者四，措置未盡善者五，宜預備者三，當善後者二。

translations.literal: The court was then intent on a major campaign. Gang, taking leave at the steps, said there were four errors in today's use of troops, five points where arrangements were not yet adequate, three things that should be prepared in advance, and two matters requiring good follow-through.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then set on a major offensive. At audience Li Gang identified four errors in current military policy, five areas where arrangements were still inadequate, three things that ought to be prepared in advance, and two matters requiring careful follow-through.

sentences.zh: 時宋師與金人、偽齊相持於淮、泗者半年，綱奏：「兩兵相持，非出奇不足以取勝。

translations.literal: At the time Song troops had faced the Jurchens and the puppet Qi along the Huai and Si for half a year. Gang memorialized: "When two armies stand locked, unless one employs the unexpected, victory cannot be won."
translations.idiomatic: Song forces had been locked in stalemate with the Jurchens and the puppet Qi along the Huai and Si rivers for half a year. Li Gang memorialized: "When two armies stand locked in stalemate, only the unexpected can secure victory."

sentences.zh: 願速遣驍將，自淮南約岳飛為掎角，夾擊之，大功可成。

translations.literal: I wish that bold generals be dispatched swiftly from Huainan to coordinate with Yue Fei in a pincer attack — great success can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that bold generals be dispatched swiftly from Huainan to coordinate with Yue Fei in a pincer attack — then great victory can be won.

sentences.zh: 」已而宋師屢捷，劉光世、張俊、楊沂中大破偽齊兵於淮、肥之上。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Song forces won repeated victories; Liu Guangshi, Zhang Jun, and Yang Qizhong utterly defeated puppet Qi troops above the Huai and Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Song forces won repeated victories, and Liu Guangshi, Zhang Jun, and Yang Qizhong routed the puppet Qi army along the Huai and Fei.

sentences.zh: 車駕進發幸建康。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage set out and proceeded to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set out and proceeded to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 綱奏乞益飭戰守之具，修築沿淮城壘，且言：「願陛下勿以去冬驟勝而自怠，勿以目前粗定而自安，凡可以致中興之治者無不為，凡可以害中興之業者無不去。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized asking to further ready equipment for battle and defense and build fortifications along the Huai, and said: "I wish Your Majesty not to grow lax from last winter's sudden victories, not to grow complacent from the present rough stability — whatever can bring restoration in governance, do all of it; whatever can harm the work of restoration, remove all of it."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang memorialized asking that equipment for battle and defense be further strengthened and fortifications built along the Huai, and said: "I pray Your Majesty will not grow lax after last winter's sudden victories, nor grow complacent because the frontier is roughly stable — do everything that can advance restoration, and remove everything that can harm it."

sentences.zh: 要以修政事，信賞罰，明是非，別邪正，招徠人材，鼓作士氣，愛惜民力，順導眾心為先。

translations.literal: The essentials are to improve government affairs, enforce rewards and punishments in trust, clarify right and wrong, distinguish the wicked from the upright, recruit talent, rouse the spirit of scholars, cherish the people's strength, and guide the common will — these come first.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, improve governance, enforce rewards and punishments faithfully, clarify right and wrong, distinguish the wicked from the upright, recruit talent, rouse morale, spare the people's strength, and guide the popular will.

sentences.zh: 數者既備，則將帥輯睦，士卒樂戰，用兵其有不勝者哉？」

translations.literal: When these several points are in place, then generals will harmonize, soldiers will delight in battle — in using troops, how could there be anyone who does not win?"
translations.idiomatic: When these are in place, generals will work in harmony, soldiers will fight willingly — and how could our armies fail to prevail?"

sentences.zh: 淮西酈瓊以全軍叛歸劉豫，綱指陳朝廷有措置失當者、深可痛惜者及當監前失以圖方來者凡十有五事，奏之。

translations.literal: In Huai West, Li Qiong defected with his entire army to Liu Yu. Gang pointed out fifteen matters — where the court's arrangements were wrong, what was deeply regrettable, and what should be learned from past errors for the future — and memorialized them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiong of Huai West defected to Liu Yu with his entire army, Li Gang identified fifteen problems — missteps in the court's handling, painful failures, and lessons to be drawn for the future — and submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 張浚引咎去相位，言者引漢武誅王恢為比。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun took blame and left the chancellorship; some memorialists compared this to Emperor Wu of Han executing Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun accepted blame and left the chancellorship; critics compared the case to Emperor Wu of Han executing Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 綱奏曰：「臣竊見張浚罷相，言者引武帝誅王恢事以為比。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized: "Your subject has seen Zhang Jun removed from the chancellorship; memorialists cite Emperor Wu's execution of Wang Hui as a parallel."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang memorialized: "I have seen Zhang Jun removed from office, with critics citing Emperor Wu's execution of Wang Hui as a parallel."

sentences.zh: 臣恐智謀之士捲舌而不談兵，忠義之士扼腕而無所發憤，將士解體而不用命，州郡望風而無堅城，陛下將誰與立國哉？

translations.literal: Your subject fears that men of strategy will roll up their tongues and speak no more of war, men of loyalty will wring their wrists with nowhere to vent their passion, troops will dissolve and obey no commands, prefectures and commanderies will watch the wind and have no stout walls — with whom will Your Majesty establish the state?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that strategists will fall silent and speak no more of war, loyal men will clench their fists with nowhere to vent their passion, troops will lose heart and refuse to obey, and prefectures will watch which way the wind blows and offer no stout defense — with whom then will Your Majesty sustain the state?

sentences.zh: 張浚措置失當，誠為有罪，然其區區徇國之心，有可矜者。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun's arrangements were indeed wrong and he is truly guilty, yet his petty heart devoted to the state has something worthy of pity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun's arrangements were indeed wrong and he was truly at fault, yet his sincere, if limited, devotion to the state deserves some compassion.

sentences.zh: 願少寬假，以責來效。」

translations.literal: I wish he may be given some leniency and held to future achievement."
translations.idiomatic: I pray he may be shown some leniency and held to future results."

sentences.zh: 時車駕將幸平江，綱以為平江去建康不遠，徒有退避之名，不宜輕動。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was about to proceed to Pingjiang. Gang thought Pingjiang was not far from Jiankang and would merely earn a name for retreat — it was not suitable to move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then about to move the court to Pingjiang. Li Gang argued that Pingjiang was not far from Jiankang and the move would earn the court nothing but a reputation for retreat — it should not be undertaken lightly.

sentences.zh: 復具奏曰：

translations.literal: He again submitted a detailed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another detailed memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞自昔用兵以成大業者，必先固人心，作士氣，據地利而不肯先退，盡人事而不肯先屈。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that from of old those who used troops to accomplish great enterprises first solidified popular resolve, roused the spirit of scholars, held advantageous ground and would not retreat first, exerted all human effort and would not yield first.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that from ancient times those who used armies to accomplish great enterprises first secured the people's loyalty, roused morale, held advantageous ground and refused to retreat first, and did all that human effort required without yielding first.

sentences.zh: 是以楚、漢相距于滎陽、成皋間，高祖雖屢敗，不退尺寸之地；

translations.literal: Therefore when Chu and Han faced each other between Xingyang and Chenggao, though Gaozu was repeatedly defeated, he did not retreat a fraction of an inch of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Chu and Han faced each other between Xingyang and Chenggao, though Emperor Gaozu suffered repeated defeats, he did not yield an inch of ground.

sentences.zh: 既割鴻溝，羽引而東，遂有垓下之亡。

translations.literal: Once the Hong Canal was divided, Xiang Yu withdrew eastward, and then came the destruction at Gaixia.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hong Canal agreement was drawn and Xiang Yu withdrew eastward, he met destruction at Gaixia.

sentences.zh: 曹操、袁紹戰於官渡，操雖兵弱糧乏，荀彧止其退避；

translations.literal: Cao Cao and Yuan Shao fought at Guandu; though Cao's troops were weak and supplies scant, Xun Yu stopped his retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao fought at Guandu, though Cao's army was weak and supplies short, Xun Yu dissuaded him from retreat.

sentences.zh: 既焚紹輜重，紹引而歸，遂喪河北。

translations.literal: Once Yuan Shao's baggage train was burned, Yuan withdrew homeward and then lost Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Shao's supply train was burned and he withdrew homeward, he lost all of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，今日之事，豈可因一叛將之故，望風怯敵，遽自退屈？

translations.literal: Viewed thus, in today's affair, how can one, because of a single defecting general, watch the wind and fear the enemy, hastily retreat and yield of oneself?
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows: how can today's crisis be met by watching which way the wind blows, fearing the enemy because one general defected, and hastily retreating?

sentences.zh: 果出此謀，六飛回馭之後，人情動搖，莫有固志，士氣銷縮，莫有鬥心。

translations.literal: If this plan is truly adopted, after the imperial carriage turns back, popular sentiment will waver and none will hold firm resolve; morale will shrink and none will have fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan is adopted, once the imperial carriage turns back popular resolve will waver and no one will stand firm; morale will collapse and no one will want to fight.

sentences.zh: 我退彼進，使敵馬南渡，得一邑則守一邑，得一州則守一州，得一路則守一路；

translations.literal: We retreat, they advance — letting enemy horsemen cross south: gain one district and hold one district, gain one prefecture and hold one prefecture, gain one circuit and hold one circuit.
translations.idiomatic: We retreat while they advance, allowing enemy cavalry to cross south — they will take each district and hold it, each prefecture and hold it, each circuit and hold it.

sentences.zh: 亂臣賊子，黠吏奸氓，從而附之，虎踞鴟張，雖欲如前日返駕還轅，復立朝廷於荊棘瓦礫之中，不可得也。

translations.literal: Rebels and traitors, cunning clerks and wicked rabble will follow and attach to them, crouching like tigers and spreading like owls — even if one wished as before to turn the carriage and return, re-establishing the court amid thorns and rubble would be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels and traitors, cunning officials and rogues will flock to them; perched like tigers and spreading like birds of prey, they will make it impossible to turn the court around as before and re-establish government amid thorns and rubble.

sentences.zh: 借使敵騎衝突，不得已而權宜避之，猶為有說。

translations.literal: Even supposing enemy cavalry should charge and break through, retreating as a temporary expedient when there is no alternative would still be defensible.
translations.idiomatic: Even if enemy cavalry broke through and a temporary withdrawal were unavoidable, that would at least be understandable.

sentences.zh: 今疆埸未有警急之報，兵將初無不利之失，朝廷正可懲往事，修軍政，審號令，明賞刑，益務固守。

translations.literal: Now the frontier has no urgent alarms, troops and generals have suffered no unfavorable setbacks — the court should just warn itself by past errors, reform military government, scrutinize commands, clarify rewards and punishments, and all the more devote itself to firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the frontier reports no urgent alarm, and troops have suffered no serious setback — the court ought instead to learn from past mistakes, reform military affairs, tighten command, clarify rewards and punishments, and devote itself all the more to holding firm.

sentences.zh: 而遽為此擾擾，棄前功，挑後患，以自趨於禍敗，豈不重可惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet hastily making this uproar, abandoning prior achievements, provoking future troubles, and rushing toward disaster and defeat — is this not doubly to be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: To rush into this turmoil instead — abandoning hard-won gains, inviting future trouble, and driving ourselves toward disaster — is this not doubly regrettable!

sentences.zh: 八年，王倫使北還，綱聞之，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Wang Lun returned from his mission north. When Gang heard of it, he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wang Lun returned from his northern mission. When Li Gang heard of it, he submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣竊見朝廷遣王倫使金國，奉迎梓宮。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen the court dispatch Wang Lun as envoy to the Jin state to escort the imperial coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: I understand the court dispatched Wang Lun as envoy to the Jin state to escort the imperial coffins home.

sentences.zh: 今倫之歸，與金使偕來，乃以「詔諭江南」為名，不著國號而曰「江南」，不雲「通問」而曰「詔諭」，此何禮也？

translations.literal: Now that Lun has returned, he comes together with Jin envoys under the title "Imperial Edict Instructing Jiangnan" — not recording the state name but saying "Jiangnan," not saying "mutual communication" but saying "imperial edict instructing" — what sort of etiquette is this?
translations.idiomatic: Now that Lun has returned alongside Jin envoys under the title "Imperial Edict Instructing Jiangnan" — using not our state's name but "Jiangnan," and not "diplomatic exchange" but "imperial edict instructing" — what kind of protocol is this?

sentences.zh: 臣請試為陛下言之。

translations.literal: Your subject asks leave to explain this to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to explain what this means, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 金人毀宗社，逼二聖，而陛下應天順人，光復舊業。

translations.literal: The Jurchens destroyed the ancestral altars, drove off the Two Sovereigns, while Your Majesty responded to Heaven and followed the people's will, restoring the old enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens ravaged our altars of state and captured the Two Sovereigns, while Your Majesty answered Heaven and the people's will and restored our heritage.

sentences.zh: 自我視彼，則仇讎也；

translations.literal: From our view of them, they are mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: In our eyes they are mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 自彼視我，則腹心之疾也，豈復有可和之理？

translations.literal: From their view of us, we are a disease of the heart and belly — how could there still be any principle of reconciliation?
translations.idiomatic: In their eyes we are a mortal affliction at the heart — how could there be any grounds for peace?

sentences.zh: 然而朝廷遣使通問，冠蓋相望於道，卑辭厚幣，無所愛惜者，以二聖在其域中，為親屈己，不得已而然，猶有說也。

translations.literal: Yet the court has sent envoys for communication, their umbrellas and canopies crowding the road, humble words and lavish gifts given without stint — because the Two Sovereigns were in their territory, yielding oneself for kin's sake when there was no alternative — this still had its rationale.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court has sent envoys to negotiate, their processions crowding the roads, humble words and lavish gifts offered without restraint — because the Two Sovereigns were held in Jin territory, and yielding for their sake when there was no alternative still had its rationale.

sentences.zh: 至去年春，兩宮凶問既至，遣使以迎梓宮，亟往遄返，初不得其要領。

translations.literal: By last spring, when news of the Two Palaces' deaths arrived, envoys were sent to escort the coffins — sent swiftly and returned swiftly, yet at first none grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: But by last spring, when news of the Two Sovereigns' deaths arrived, envoys were sent to escort the coffins — sent in haste and returned in haste, yet grasped nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 今倫使事，初以奉迎梓宮為指，而金使之來，乃以詔諭江南為名。

translations.literal: Now Lun's mission was initially directed at escorting the coffins home, yet the Jin envoys who came were under the name of instructing Jiangnan by imperial edict.
