translations.idiomatic: Lun's mission was initially framed as escorting the coffins home, yet the Jin envoys who came did so under the title of "imperial edict instructing Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 循名責實，已自乖戾，則其所以罔朝廷而生後患者，不待詰而可知。

translations.literal: Judging the name and demanding the reality, they are already at odds — then the way they will deceive the court and breed future troubles needs no inquiry to be known.
translations.idiomatic: Judging name against reality, the discrepancy is already plain — and one need not probe deeply to see how the court will be deceived and future trouble bred.

sentences.zh: 臣在遠方，雖不足以知其曲折，然以愚意料之，金以此名遣使，其邀求大略有五：必降詔書，欲陛下屈體降禮以聽受，一也。

translations.literal: Your subject is in a distant place and though insufficient to know all its twists, yet by dull reasoning I judge: the Jin, sending envoys under this title, have roughly five demands — they will surely deliver an edict, wishing Your Majesty to abase your person and lower ritual to receive it — first.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am far away and cannot know every detail, I can infer this much: sending envoys under this title, the Jin have roughly five demands — they will require the issuance of an edict for Your Majesty to receive with abased status and lowered ritual — first.

sentences.zh: 必有赦文，欲朝廷宣佈，班示郡縣，二也。

translations.literal: There will surely be an amnesty decree, wishing the court to proclaim it and display it in prefectures and districts — second.
translations.idiomatic: They will require an amnesty decree for the court to proclaim throughout the prefectures and districts — second.

sentences.zh: 必立約束，欲陛下奉藩稱臣，稟其號令，三也。

translations.literal: There will surely be binding agreements, wishing Your Majesty to serve as a vassal and call yourself subject, obeying their commands — third.
translations.idiomatic: They will require binding agreements for Your Majesty to serve as a vassal king and accept subject status, obeying their commands — third.

sentences.zh: 必求歲賂，廣其數目，使我坐困，四也。

translations.literal: They will surely demand annual tribute, expanding the amounts, to leave us sitting in exhaustion — fourth.
translations.idiomatic: They will demand annual tribute at increased levels to exhaust us financially — fourth.

sentences.zh: 必求割地，以江為界，淮南、荊襄、四川，盡欲得之，五也。

translations.literal: They will surely demand ceded territory, taking the river as boundary — Huainan, Jingxiang, Sichuan — they wish to obtain all — fifth.
translations.idiomatic: They will demand territorial concessions with the Yangtze as the boundary — Huainan, Jing-Xiang, and Sichuan — all of which they want to seize — fifth.

sentences.zh: 此五者，朝廷從其一，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Of these five, if the court accedes to even one, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If the court accedes to even one of these five demands, the great enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 金人變詐不測，貪婪無厭，縱使聽其詔令，奉藩稱臣，其志猶未已也。

translations.literal: The Jurchens are unpredictable in deceit and insatiable in greed; even if one obeys their edicts and serves as a vassal and calls oneself subject, their ambition still will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens are treacherous beyond prediction and insatiable in greed; even if we obey their edicts and accept vassal status, their ambitions will not cease.

sentences.zh: 必繼有號令，或使親迎梓宮，或使單車入覲，或使移易將相，或改革政事，或竭取租賦，或朘削土宇。

translations.literal: Commands will surely follow in succession — perhaps requiring one to escort the coffins in person, to enter court alone in a single carriage, to replace generals and chancellors, to reform government affairs, to drain tax revenues, or to pare away territory.
translations.idiomatic: More demands will surely follow — that we escort the imperial coffins in person, enter court alone in a single carriage, replace generals and ministers, reform government policy, drain our tax revenues, or whittle away our territory.

sentences.zh: 從之則無有紀極，一不從則前功盡廢，反為兵端。

translations.literal: If one accedes, there is no limit; if one refuses even once, prior achievements are wholly undone and war becomes the consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Obey and there will be no end to it; refuse even once and all prior gains are lost — and war will follow.

sentences.zh: 以為權時之宜，聽其邀求，可以無後悔者，非愚則誣也。

translations.literal: To think that as a temporary expedient one may heed their demands and be without later regret — such a man is either a fool or a deceiver.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever thinks that yielding to their demands as a temporary expedient can be done without regret is either a fool or a liar.

sentences.zh: 使國家之勢單弱，果不足以自振，不得已而為此，固猶不可，況土宇之廣猶半天下，臣民之心戴宋不忘，與有識者謀之，尚足以有為，豈可忘祖宗之大業，生靈之屬望，弗慮弗圖，遽自屈服，冀延旦暮之命哉？

translations.literal: Supposing the state's power were isolated and weak and truly insufficient to revive itself, and one had no choice but to do this — even then it would still be wrong; how much more when our territory still spans half the realm, the hearts of officials and people still honor the Song without forgetting, and with men of insight to plan with us we are still sufficient to act — how can one forget the great enterprise of the ancestors and the hopes of the living, fail to consider or plan, hastily submit of oneself, and hope only to prolong one's days?
translations.idiomatic: Even if our power were truly too weak to recover on our own and such submission were unavoidable, it would still be wrong — how much more so when our lands still span half the realm, the people still hold to the Song in their hearts, and with men of insight we could still act? How can we forget the great enterprise of our ancestors and the hopes of the people, fail to plan or consider, and hastily yield ourselves merely to prolong our days?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下特留聖意，且勿輕許，深詔群臣，講明利害、可以久長之策，擇其善而從之。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty especially to reserve your sacred judgment, and for the present not lightly consent; deeply instruct the ministers to debate gains and losses and policies that can endure long, and choose what is good and follow it.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will hold your sacred judgment in reserve and not lightly consent; deeply instruct your ministers to debate the gains and losses and the policies that can endure, and choose what is best.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，雖與眾論不合，不上以為忤，曰：「大臣當如此矣。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, though it did not accord with prevailing opinion, the emperor did not take it as insubordination, saying: "A chief minister ought to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, though it ran against prevailing opinion, the emperor did not take it as insubordination, saying: "A chief minister ought to speak like this."

sentences.zh: 九年，除知潭州、荊湖南路安撫大使，綱具奏力辭，曰：「臣迂疏無周身之術，動致煩言。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou and Grand Commissioner for Pacification of Jinghu South Circuit. Gang submitted a detailed memorial vigorously declining, saying: "Your subject is narrow and impractical, with no art of self-preservation, and constantly provokes troublesome talk."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou and Grand Commissioner for Pacification of Jinghu South Circuit. Li Gang submitted a detailed memorial vigorously declining, saying: "Your servant is narrow-minded and impractical, with no art of self-preservation, and my actions constantly draw censure."

sentences.zh: 今者罷自江西，為日未久，又蒙湔祓，畀以帥權。

translations.literal: Now, dismissed from Jiangxi not long ago, I have again been washed clean and granted command over armies.
translations.idiomatic: I was recently dismissed from Jiangxi, and scarcely any time has passed before I am rehabilitated and given command over armies.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝聞季布賢，召之，既而罷歸，布曰：'陛下以一人之譽召臣，一人之毀去臣，臣恐天下有以窺陛下之淺深。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han heard that Ji Bu was worthy and summoned him; soon afterward he was dismissed and sent home. Ji Bu said: "Your Majesty summoned your subject on one man's praise and dismissed him on one man's slander — I fear the realm will infer the depth or shallowness of Your Majesty's judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han heard that Ji Bu was worthy and summoned him; soon afterward he was dismissed and sent home. Ji Bu said: "Your Majesty summoned me on one man's praise and dismissed me on one man's slander — I fear the realm will read the depth or shallowness of Your Majesty's judgment."

sentences.zh: '顧臣區區進退，何足少多。

translations.literal: "As for your subject's petty comings and goings, they are scarcely worth mentioning."
translations.idiomatic: "As for my petty comings and goings, they matter little in themselves."

sentences.zh: 然數年之間，亟奮亟躓，上累陛下知人任使之明，實有系於國體。

translations.literal: Yet within a few years, repeatedly raised up and repeatedly cast down, this reflects on Your Majesty's discernment in knowing men and assigning roles — it truly bears on the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a few years I have been raised up and cast down in rapid succession — this reflects on Your Majesty's discernment in knowing men and assigning roles, and truly bears on the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 」詔以綱累奏，不欲重違，遂允其請。

translations.literal: An edict noted that Gang had memorialized repeatedly; not wishing to gainsay him further, the emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Li Gang had memorialized repeatedly; unwilling to gainsay him further, the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 次年薨，年五十八。

translations.literal: The following year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上為軫悼，遣使賻贈，撫問其家，給喪葬之費。

translations.literal: When news of his death arrived, the emperor mourned deeply, dispatched envoys with condolence gifts, sent condolences to his family, and provided funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death arrived, the emperor mourned deeply, dispatched envoys with condolence gifts, sent condolences to his family, and provided funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，官其親族十人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Preceptor, and ten of his kin were granted official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Preceptor, and ten members of his family were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 綱負天下之望，以一身用舍為社稷生民安危。

translations.literal: Gang bore the hopes of the empire; whether he himself was employed or dismissed was tied to the safety of state altars and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang bore the hopes of the empire; whether he was employed or dismissed was bound up with the safety of state and people.

sentences.zh: 雖身或不用，用有不久，而其忠誠義氣，凜然動乎遠邇。

translations.literal: Though he himself was sometimes not used, or used only briefly, his loyal integrity and righteous spirit stirred awe near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was sometimes not employed, or employed only briefly, his loyal integrity and righteous spirit stirred awe near and far.

sentences.zh: 每宋使至燕山，必問李綱、趙鼎安否，其為遠人所畏服如此。

translations.literal: Whenever Song envoys reached Yan Mountain, they were always asked whether Li Gang and Zhao Ding were safe and well — such was the awe he inspired among distant men.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Song envoys reached Yan Mountain, they were always asked whether Li Gang and Zhao Ding were safe and well — such was the awe he inspired among distant foes.

sentences.zh: 綱有著《易傳》內篇十卷、外篇十二卷，《論語詳說》十卷，文章、歌詩、奏議百餘卷，又有《靖康傳信錄》、《奉迎錄》、《建炎時政記》、《建炎進退志》、《建炎制詔表劄集》、《宣撫荊廣記》、《制置江右錄》。

translations.literal: Gang authored the Inner Chapters of his Commentary on the Changes in ten scrolls and the Outer Chapters in twelve scrolls, Detailed Expositions on the Analects in ten scrolls, more than a hundred scrolls of essays, songs, poems, and memorials, and also Records of Trust in the Jingkang Crisis, Records of the Imperial Welcome, Records of Jianyan Government, Records of Advance and Retreat in the Jianyan Era, Collected Jianyan Edicts and Memorials, Records of Pacification in Jing and Guang, and Records of Military Affairs in Jiang Right.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang authored the Inner Chapters of his Commentary on the Changes in ten volumes and the Outer Chapters in twelve, Detailed Expositions on the Analects in ten volumes, and more than a hundred volumes of essays, poems, and memorials, as well as Records of Trust in the Jingkang Crisis, Records of the Imperial Welcome, Records of Jianyan Government, Records of Advance and Retreat in the Jianyan Era, Collected Jianyan Edicts and Memorials, Records of Pacification in Jing and Guang, and Records of Military Affairs in Jiang Right.

sentences.zh: 論曰：以李綱之賢，使得畢力殫慮于靖康、建炎間，莫或撓之，二帝何至於北行，而宋豈至為南渡之偏安哉？

translations.literal: The historians comment: With a man as worthy as Li Gang, had he been allowed to exhaust his strength and wisdom between the Jingkang and Jianyan reigns without anyone obstructing him, how would the Two Sovereigns have been driven north, and how would Song have been reduced to the partial security of the south after crossing the river?
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: With a man as worthy as Li Gang, had he been allowed to exhaust his strength and wisdom between the Jingkang and Jianyan reigns without obstruction, how would the Two Sovereigns have been driven north, and how would Song have been reduced to the partial sway of the south?

sentences.zh: 夫用君子則安，用小人則危，不易之理也。

translations.literal: Employ the noble and the state is secure; employ the base and the state is endangered — this principle does not change.
translations.idiomatic: Employ the upright and the state is secure; employ the corrupt and the state is endangered — this principle does not change.

sentences.zh: 人情莫不喜安而惡危。

translations.literal: Among human feelings, none fails to love security and hate peril.
translations.idiomatic: None among men fails to love security and hate peril.

sentences.zh: 然綱居相位僅七十日，其謀數不見用，獨于黃潛善、汪伯彥、秦檜之言，信而任之，恒若不及，何高宗之見，與人殊哉？

translations.literal: Yet Gang held the chancellorship for barely seventy days, and his counsels were repeatedly not adopted — while Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, and Qin Hui alone were trusted and entrusted, as though there were no time to lose. How strange that Gaozong's vision differed from ordinary men's!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Gang held the chancellorship for barely seventy days, and his counsels were repeatedly rejected — while Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, and Qin Hui alone were trusted and entrusted as though there were no time to lose. How strange that Gaozong's vision differed so from ordinary men's!

sentences.zh: 綱雖屢斥，忠誠不少貶，不以用舍為語默，若赤子之慕其母，怒呵猶噭々焉挽其裳裾而從之。

translations.literal: Though Gang was repeatedly dismissed, his loyalty was not diminished; he did not choose silence or speech according to whether he was employed — like an infant clinging to its mother, even when scolded and shouted at he still cried out and tugged at her hem as he followed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Gang was repeatedly dismissed, his loyalty was not diminished; he did not choose silence or speech according to whether he was employed — like an infant clinging to its mother, he still cried out and tugged at her hem even when scolded and shouted at.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，中興功業之不振，君子固歸之天，若綱之心，其可謂非諸葛孔明之用心歟？

translations.literal: Alas — that the work of restoration did not flourish, upright men may indeed ascribe to Heaven; yet as for Gang's heart, can it be said to fall short of Zhuge Kongming's devotion?
translations.idiomatic: Alas, that the work of restoration did not flourish — upright men may indeed ascribe this to Heaven; yet can Li Gang's devotion be said to fall short of Zhuge Kongming's?
